title: The Depression, King of Jazz and its Roxy flop
summary: The picture was a bust and the Roxy show with Gershwin drew nobody, ending the band's good run.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: So they went out and then they made the picture so I had nothing to do with it. I wasn't in it. I wasn't around when it was done, and they were doing, now, they're doing the Old Gold Show, doing them all from the road, and at the same time business is getting worse and worse and we have had the Wall Street crash.

The Depression has set in. It had set in and went on for a years, you see, before it bothered us. In other words, there were the theatres that they could do, there were the records, but the records were falling off and we had gone over to Columbia. The Victor records, and then the European trip had been cancelled and the picture was a sort of a bust.
Was I talking about the band went out.
Yeah, you said the picture was a bust.
Well, anyway, the band came back and they played down here at Valley Stream, played a few dates and
waiting for the picture, the release of the picture.

That's the date I received. 1930, in June. It came to the Roxy and at that time Paul had been complaining about the band, that the band business was lousy and the only thing that he was depending on mostly was the Old Gold Show and well, anyway, they brought the picture into the Roxy, it could have been May, but anyway at that particular time, they brought it into the Roxy, and Gershwin appeared with them and the Rhythm Boys had not come back with them now, which probably doesn't make any difference, as far as this is the Whiteman thing, but the -- I remember going to the show, the band was there a week and Gershwin had appeared -- they put the show on for a whole week and they didn't draw anybody. It flopped. The whole thing flopped, and they made up their minds by the end of the week that they would continue without the band and just Gershwin would be there to play the "Rhapsody," and they were showing the picture.
